{{Short description|Brazilian physicist and radio astronomer}}
{{Distinguish|Pierre Koffmann}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=August 2021}}
'''Pierre Kaufmann''' (1938 – 17 February 2017) was a French physicist and astronomer. He worked at Mackenzie University, Unicamp, and USP, and founded research into radio astronomy and solar physics in Brazil.

== Career ==
He studied physics at [[Mackenzie Presbyterian University]],<ref name="ABC_2017" /> starting in 1957,<ref name="revisitapesquisa" /> and graduating in 1961,<ref name="fapesp_2017" /> before going to [[Leiden University]] and [[Groningen University]].<ref name="ABC_2017" />

He was the principal researcher of the [[Solar Submillimeter Telescope]] and [[Solar-T]], and started the Atmospheric Science program at the [[Brazilian Antarctic Program]]. He founded research into radio astronomy, spatial geodesy, and solar physics in Brazil.<ref name="ABC_2017" /> He helped install the first radio telescope in Brazil in 1962,<ref name="revisitapesquisa" /> at the [[Professor Aristóteles Orsini Planetarium]], but the antenna was subsequently destroyed by cows. He was funded by [[FAPESP]] is its first year of operation, to work on radio star scintillation.<ref name="fapesp_2017" /> He also helped construct radio telescopes in [[Campos do Jordão]] and at [[Itapetinga Radio Observatory]].<ref name="fapesp_2017" />

He was a professor at the [[Mackenzie Presbyterian University]]<ref name="ABC_2017" /> since 1998,<ref name="ABC_member" />  where he was coordinator for the [[Center for Radio Astronomy and Astrophysics]],<ref name="fapesp_2017" /> and a senior researcher at the [[Centre for Semiconductor Components]] (Portuguese: Centro de Componentes Semicondutores)<ref name="ABC_2017" /> at [[UNICAMP]], as well as an associate professor at the [[Polytechnic School of the University of São Paulo]]. He published over 200 papers, and supervised 17 Masters students, 7 PhD students, and 8 postdocs.<ref name="fapesp_2017" />

He was also the president of the [[URSI]] Brazilian National Committee between 1989 and 2009.<ref name="ABC_2017" /> He was a member of the [[IAU]],<ref name="iau" /> [[COSPAR]],<ref name="ABC_2017" /> the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]] (since 1987),<ref name="ABC_member" /> and the [[Brazilian Astronomical Society]].<ref name="fapesp_2017" /> He was an associate member of the [[Royal Astronomical Society]].<ref name="ABC_member" />

== Personal life ==
Kaufman was born in 1938.<ref name="iau" /> He grew up on a farm in [[Aix-en-Provence]], south France,<ref name="revisitapesquisa" /> and became interested in astronomy as a child.<ref name="fapesp_2017" /> His family moved to Brazil in 1941, fleeing [[World War II]].<ref name="revisitapesquisa" /> He joined the [[Association of Amateur Astronomers]] as a teenager, in 1954.<ref name="fapesp_2017" /> He had a brother.<ref name="revisitapesquisa" />

He died in [[São Paulo]]<ref name="revisitapesquisa" /> on 17 February 2017,<ref name="ABC_2017" /> aged 78.<ref name="fapesp_2017" />
